sections.heading: Interstate driving, rural roads and trip planning
sections.markdown:
# Interstate driving, rural roads and trip planning

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
Approach an uncontrolled rural junction slowly and be ready for crossing traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
Expect farm equipment, school buses, people and animals near hidden rural driveways or junctions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
Deer-crossing signs warn of an area where animal encounters deserve extra caution. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A01
Wildlife is often active near dawn and dusk, when visibility also changes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A01
If one animal is near the road, be prepared for others nearby. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A01
Scan ahead and along both road edges in wildlife areas. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A01
Do not swerve into opposing traffic or off the roadway to avoid an animal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A02
Slow near animals beside the road because they may suddenly change direction or enter it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A02
The guide recommends reporting a collision involving a large wild or farm animal to police. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A02
A reflective or fluorescent orange-and-red triangle on a slow vehicle warns that it travels below twenty-five miles per hour. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A02
Farm machinery may be wide enough to occupy more than one traffic lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A02
A farm-machine operator may swing left before making a right turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A02
Pass slow farm equipment cautiously rather than assume its operator hears an approaching vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-R14 | anchor: A02
Animal-drawn vehicles have a right to use the road and must follow applicable traffic rules. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-R15 | anchor: A03
Large loads can prevent an animal-drawn vehicle’s driver from seeing traffic behind. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R16 | anchor: A03
Do not sound the horn or rev the engine when passing an animal-drawn vehicle because it may frighten the animal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R17 | anchor: A03
Expect an animal-drawn vehicle to turn into a field or driveway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R18 | anchor: A03
Approach a ridden or led horse at a reasonable speed and leave reasonable distance. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R19 | anchor: A03
Do not use a loud horn or engine noise near a horse being ridden or led beside the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R20 | anchor: A03
A slow driver delaying following traffic should let it pass from a safe place at the roadside. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R21 | anchor: A03
Overloading can impair stopping and damage vehicle suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R22 | anchor: A03
Before towing, determine the trailer’s empty weight, load capacity and the vehicle’s combined weight rating. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R23 | anchor: A03
In heavy rain or fog, slow and use low beams. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R24 | anchor: A03
If fog prevents adequate vision, leave the highway at the nearest safe stopping place rather than continue creeping along it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R25 | anchor: A04
Use low beams while following another vehicle, in heavy traffic, fog, snowfall or heavy rain. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R26 | anchor: A04
High beams can reflect from precipitation or fog and increase glare. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R27 | anchor: A04
Avoid staring into an approaching headlight beam and do not retaliate with bright lights. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R28 | anchor: A04
Do not wear tinted glasses or sunglasses at night because they reduce available vision. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R29 | anchor: A04
Night travel requires a speed that allows stopping within the illuminated distance. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R30 | anchor: A04
The guide recommends at least four seconds of following room on a rural road at night. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R31 | anchor: A04
An open driving zone has available travel space; a closed zone has a restriction on travel or visibility. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R32 | anchor: A04
Changing conditions can alter speed, visibility, lane width, traffic flow or available space. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R33 | anchor: A05
Lower speed in a busy urban environment provides more time to identify hazards and decide on a response. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R34 | anchor: A05
Combine errands or share rides where possible to reduce trips and traffic exposure. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R35 | anchor: A05
For trip planning, consider route numbers, entrances, exits, fuel, rest stops and construction. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R36 | anchor: A05
Before a trip, inspect windows, lights, tires, fluid levels, belts, hoses and brakes. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R37 | anchor: A06
Carry insurance information, the vehicle manual, local maps and funds for unexpected trip expenses. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-R38 | anchor: A06
The guide recommends an extra set of keys for loss or accidental lockout during travel. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0114]
